engagement_title: Nordhaven direct-booking launch: one committed tone across a two-visit property shoot, amenity cut-outs that hold on the near-black booking page, fourteen room cards merged off last season's printed card, and the lookbook set handed back editable
vertical: Hospitality and travel: a fourteen-room design-led micro-hotel in a converted harbour warehouse, opening its own direct-booking channel after three years of selling only through the large travel platforms
real_brief_anchor: Ledger anchor for PHOTO-22. This id carries an EMPTY real_brief_anchors array in the ledger, so there is no marketplace grounding note to quote and none is invented here. The anchor is the ledger concept itself, quoted verbatim: one_line_ask, 'Give our micro design-hotel a distinctive, moody signature image treatment for the lookbook and social, a single stylized tone that runs across every amenity and detail shot so it looks unmistakably like us and nothing like a generic booking listing'; price_demo, 'A design-led micro-hotel at $600/night for design-literate 30-45 urban travellers who choose on aesthetic; a committed, restrained monochromatic signature is load-bearing.' The verdict is REBUILD because that concept, as banked, ended in one tinted image set plus crops of it, which is one deliverable and one surface. The fuller commission a property in this position actually buys, and the shape these jobs are posted in on the freelance marketplaces (a launch kit rather than a retouch), is the one built here: the signature committed across a shoot that happened on two different visits, the amenity objects cut out for the near-black booking page, the lookbook and social canvases handed back editable because the room list changes, and the desk room-directory cards reprinted off last season's press file against a new rate sheet. The hotel is the fictional Nordhaven, in a converted harbour warehouse; no real property, platform, brand or person is referenced.
client_one_liner: Our pictures sit in a grid next to three hundred other properties and look exactly like them, the shoot happened over two visits that do not match, and every cut-out we have tried looks fine until it goes on the dark booking page.
client_brief:
We are a fourteen-room hotel in a converted harbour warehouse and we open for direct bookings in eleven weeks. Right now every guest reaches us through the large travel platforms, where our pictures sit in a grid next to three hundred other properties and look exactly like them. That is the whole problem. People choose us because of how the building feels, and the pictures carry none of it.

I want one tone. A single committed treatment across every amenity and detail shot, so that when somebody sees three of our pictures anywhere they know they are ours before they read the name. Moody, restrained, a little cold. We are not a bright and cheerful place and I do not want to pretend we are.

There is one exception. The main room photograph on the booking page stays true colour, because a guest spending six hundred a night wants to know what the bed and the linen actually look like. Everything else can carry the tone.

The shoot happened over two visits, one in autumn and one in winter. They do not match. I am told that is normal.

Three things sit on our booking page against a near-black background: the carafe, the robe and the brass key fob. I need those cut out properly. Every attempt we have made looks perfectly fine until it goes on the dark, and then you can see exactly where it was cut.

For the lookbook I need a spread, plus a squarer social version and a full-height story version, and I want those in one file I can edit myself, because the room list changes.

Last thing, the room directory cards on the desks. I have last year's print file and a spreadsheet of the fourteen rooms with the new rates and views. Same card, new content, ready for the printer.

What I need back: the finished set, the cut-outs, the lookbook file, the room cards, a board my partner can review, and a note on what you did.
price_band_and_audience: Design-led micro-hotel, six hundred dollars a night, sold direct to design-literate 30 to 45 urban travellers who choose a property on aesthetic and book it because it looks like nowhere else. The band is load-bearing on nearly every decision in the job. At this level a committed, restrained, near-monochromatic signature is the product: the guest is buying atmosphere and a point of view, so the treatment has to be strong enough to survive being seen three pictures at a time in someone's feed. Run the same commission for a one hundred and twenty dollar highway property and every choice inverts: that booker needs bright, literal, reassuring colour and a clear picture of the bed, and this moody tint would actively lose them. The band also decides where the tone stops. The one true-colour room hero exists because a guest paying this much wants to see the actual linen, and an agent that tints it for consistency has followed the pattern and broken the commission. The same restraint governs the collateral: air, one photograph doing the work, type that does not shout, rates set quietly rather than as offers. Cheerful, saturated, discount-shaped design at this price reads as a property pretending to be something it is not. The ledger records the base treatment at 400 to 900 dollars; this full launch commission, with the cut-outs, the editable canvases and the fourteen-record card run, sits at 1,400 to 2,600 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.tagline: A room with the harbour in it
brand_identity.sector: A fourteen-room design-led micro-hotel in a converted harbour warehouse, sold direct.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Opened 2023 on the Nordhavn waterfront, Copenhagen; fourteen rooms run by one small owner-led team.
brand_identity.about: Nordhaven is a fourteen-room hotel inside a converted brick and timber warehouse on the working harbour. We sell the feeling of the building: cold light, plaster, oak and brass. Guests choose us because the place looks like nowhere else, and everything we make has to carry that.
brand_identity.audience: Design-literate urban travellers, 30 to 45, who choose a property on aesthetic and book direct once they trust the point of view.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Six hundred dollars a night, direct only, positioned above the travel-platform grid as a design destination rather than a room count.
brand_identity.typography: A quiet high-contrast serif for display, set large and used sparingly, with a clean neutral grotesque for text. Nothing shouts, and rates sit small.
brand_identity.voice: Spare, understated, first person, no exclamation. Example line: 'Fourteen rooms on the water. We open direct booking this autumn.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: We work from a short brand note that fixes the near-black ground, the placements and the delivered sizes. There is no full guideline system yet, and the room list changes each season.
brand_identity.values: One committed tone across everything, with the true-colour main room photograph kept as the single deliberate exception so guests see the actual bed and linen.

assets_supplied.name: nordhaven_property_shoot/ (16 frames, 4,200 to 5,000px long edge)
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Amenity and detail shots plus the rooms, from two visits, one in autumn and one in winter. They do not match." Bath and bedside details, the breakfast counter, the stair, the harbour window, plus one full-frame room.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two things nobody in the hotel can see. First, two of the detail frames separate their subject from their ground almost entirely by hue rather than by value (a moss-green wool throw lying on an oak-grey bench, a terracotta cup on a rust-red tray), so any single tone ramp collapses both of them into one flat field, while each still looks plausible on its own at thumbnail size. Second, the winter visit was shot after the blinds were replaced, so those six frames sit a step darker in the shadows than the autumn ones and plug solid once a tint is committed on top of an uncorrected base.

assets_supplied.name: nordhaven_amenity_objects/ (3 frames, 4,600px)
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The carafe, the folded robe and the brass key fob, shot on our own surfaces so they would look at home." One object per frame, styled on the hotel's plaster and oak.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The unglazed carafe is photographed against the hotel's own limewashed plaster and its shadow side sits at almost exactly the plaster's value, so an automatic knockout succeeds, returns a clean-looking file, and quietly bites the lip and the shoulder away on that side. The key fob is the opposite problem: its plate carries an enclosed cut-out letterform that a background removal cannot punch at all, so that route returns the hole filled with captured oak while reporting success.

assets_supplied.name: nordhaven_room_card_2025.pdf
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Last year's room directory card, the file the printer used." A real press PDF of a single-sided card carrying the room name, the floor and bed line, the view line and the nightly rate, printed and font-embedded.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two things the printed page does not reveal. The card's copy was set around the shortest room name the hotel had last year, so the name frame has very little slack at the merged type size, and InDesign does not spill an over-long merged record, it simply stops rendering it at the frame edge with no warning anywhere. And the four visual blocks on the printed card do not correspond to four converted frames: the conversion's real granularity is a property of how the PDF was drawn, not of how the card looks.

assets_supplied.name: nordhaven_rooms.csv
assets_supplied.visible_description: The fourteen rooms with name, floor, bed type, view line, nightly rate and an image column naming the frame each card should carry.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Three of the fourteen rooms were renamed this season and now carry two-word names roughly half again as long as anything on last year's card, and their view lines are longer again. The rate column is also inconsistently typed across the rows, which is a copy decision the agent has to make rather than a defect any tool reports.

assets_supplied.name: nordhaven_brand_notes.txt
assets_supplied.visible_description: The near-black ground the booking page and the lookbook cover use, the placements and the delivered size each one is used at, the price band and who books, and the note that the main room photograph on the booking page stays true colour.

acceptance_bar: The tinted set reads as one committed treatment seen three pictures at a time, with no frame jumping against its neighbours and no frame collapsing into a flat field.
The two visits are indistinguishable in the finished set. Nothing gives away that the shoot happened twice.
The one true-colour room hero for the booking page is delivered untinted, and nothing else in the set is.

The three amenity cut-outs hold their edges on the near-black ground the booking page uses, judged on that ground and not on white, with nothing bitten out of an edge and no enclosed interior left filled.
No invented pixels anywhere. No delivered file exceeds its source dimensions, and the note lists every picture any tool resized, downscaled or extended, and by how much.
Every crop is composed for the size it is actually used at rather than scaled down from one master.
The lookbook spread, the social canvas and the story canvas sit in ONE editable file, each keeping its own canvas size, delivered with the self-contained source it was built from.
The words in that file are live text the client can retype, and every photograph in it is a real photograph rather than an empty frame.
One type system across all three canvases, with the note naming per role the family, its foundry or designer, and the weight actually used.
Fourteen room cards, one record per page, in the printer's order, every card carrying the correct room's photograph rather than one image repeated.
Every field on every card is fully present at trim. No name, view line or rate is cut off, and nothing that was mapped is silently missing.
Anything licensed sits with the property's own photography rather than reading as a bought picture.
The board carries the finished set with nothing silently dropped.
The note states, per frame, what was applied, and names any frame that could not be brought into the set and what happened to the placement it was carrying.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle what lands where: the pictures and the cut-outs on imaging, the three canvases on HTML authoring, the fourteen cards on the merge path.
trajectory.judgement: The temptation is to read this as a tint job with some crops attached. The real structure is that two of the five deliverables are defined by a surface they must survive (a near-black ground, a printed trim) rather than by a look.
trajectory.produces: A plan naming deliverable to surface and the confirmed tier.

trajectory.action: Upload the sixteen shoot frames, the three object frames, last season's card PDF and the room sheet, holding a manifest with source dimensions.
trajectory.judgement: Source dimensions are recorded here because every no-invented-pixels claim later is made against them.
trajectory.produces: A manifest with source dimensions and a presigned URL per file.

trajectory.action: Preview all nineteen frames and triage: which visit each came from, how each frame's subject separates from its ground, how much room sits around the subject, and which single frame is the true-colour booking hero that must be held out of the treatment.
trajectory.judgement: Identifying the exception before committing to the signature. The brief names it in one sentence in the middle of a paragraph about tone, and an agent working from the headline ask will tint all sixteen.
trajectory.produces: A per-frame triage note and the named exception.

trajectory.action: Straighten where needed and bring both visits onto one base: correct exposure, neutral and shadow depth per frame so autumn and winter start from the same place, one call per frame, recording parameters.
trajectory.judgement: A tint applied on top of two different bases produces two different results from one setting. The correction has to happen before the style, and the two halves need different corrections to arrive at the same base.
trajectory.produces: Nineteen corrected frames on one base with a per-frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Masked work where a whole-frame move is wrong: correct plaster, oak and linen separately by naming the material rather than the object sitting on it.
trajectory.judgement: Prompt wording is the entire gate here. Naming the substrate returns the substrate; naming a material's own visual properties returns the material. Plaster and oak want opposite moves that cannot both be served globally.
trajectory.produces: Corrected frames where a global move would have taken the plaster green or the oak grey.

trajectory.action: Commit the signature: choose the tint hue, the tint strength and the grain, apply across the set one frame at a time, and hold the booking hero out of it entirely.
trajectory.judgement: How far the tone goes is the design decision the whole engagement turns on, and at this band it is a question of restraint rather than of strength. Batching one identical parameter set across frames that arrived from two visits is the fast answer and it is the wrong one.
trajectory.produces: A tinted and grained master set plus one untinted true-colour hero, with applied settings recorded.

trajectory.action: Lay the tinted set out together at lookbook reproduction size and look across it rather than at each file in turn.
trajectory.judgement: Deciding to view the set as a set is the agent's own move; nothing prompts it, and every individual file looks correct.
trajectory.produces: A verdict on the set as a set.

trajectory.action: Take the three amenity objects to transparency, choosing a route per object rather than a route for the batch, and produce the near-black composited versions the booking page needs.
trajectory.judgement: The three objects look like one job and are not. An object whose plate carries an enclosed cut-out cannot be knocked out by background removal at all, and the correct route for it is to select the ground material, invert and fill, which is a different operation on a different principle.
trajectory.produces: Three transparent cut-outs plus their composited-on-black versions.

trajectory.action: Composite each cut-out onto the exact near-black ground the booking page uses and inspect the edges close up.
trajectory.judgement: This is the only place the edges can be judged. Both failure modes are invisible on white, which is precisely why every attempt the hotel made looked fine to them.
trajectory.produces: An edge verdict per object on the ground that matters.

trajectory.action: Search Stock with short generic queries for a night harbour or warehouse exterior, filter to photography, exclude generative results, license and download at full resolution, then bring it toward the committed tone and lay it beside the set.
trajectory.judgement: Under a committed single tone what decides whether a licensed frame joins is its luminance structure and its black point, not its colour, and a 240 pixel thumbnail carries evidence about neither.
trajectory.produces: One licensed camera-scale exterior, tinted to the set and judged against it.

trajectory.action: Compose the placement crops: the lookbook spread ratio, the 4:5 social and the 9:16 story, each framed for the size it is used at, reading each crop's tradeoff metadata and extending a frame at its edges rather than interpolating where a placement needs more room than the frame holds.
trajectory.judgement: A spread and a story are not one crop scaled. The tradeoffs array is the only signal that a crop interpolated, and adding edge material is the only route that does not invent detail inside the frame.
trajectory.produces: Composed crops per placement with a resize and extension record.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per typographic role, read the family style inventories for real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own art direction and has to read at six hundred a night. Weight cannot be inferred from a style name, a display cut is reached by its own family slug, and one bad name in the kit call discards the valid ones with it.
trajectory.produces: A one-kit type system with family, foundry or designer and real weight per role.

trajectory.action: Author one self-contained HTML with three roots at three canvas sizes: the lookbook spread, the 4:5 social and the 9:16 story. Embed every photograph as image data, anchor every element from the top left with explicit sizes, and declare family and weight on every text element.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a URL is not a photograph on this importer, weight is not inherited from markup semantics, and a global canvas override collapses a mixed-size set. The design work is how much air each canvas carries at this band.
trajectory.produces: One export-ready HTML carrying all three canvases, uploaded and addressable, retained as a deliverable in its own right.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export, then verify through both channels that exist: resolve the document's rendition and look at the first canvas, and parse the returned per-canvas markup for the other two, asserting per canvas that every photograph resolved to real image data, that the type resolved to the licensed faces, and that nothing sits beyond its declared canvas width.
trajectory.judgement: Treating a successful export as unverified. Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the rendition only ever shows the first canvas.
trajectory.produces: A native editable document with three canvases, an inspected first canvas and a markup audit of the other two.

trajectory.action: Convert last season's card PDF to a live document, export IDML, and actually look at what came back: how many text frames exist, what each one holds, and whether the story text the mapping readout reports matches the story the document contains.
trajectory.judgement: The printed card shows four separate blocks, which is not evidence about frames. What the conversion exposes decides whether per-frame mapping is available at all or whether everything has to be done by offset inside one story, and that determines the entire mapping strategy.
trajectory.produces: A true frame inventory and a reconstructed story text.

trajectory.action: Build the mapping against the reconstructed story, validate it, prepare the merge template, then re-export IDML and confirm every expected placeholder is genuinely present rather than trusting the success message.
trajectory.judgement: Both the validator and the prepare step report success on mappings that never landed, so the only evidence that a field exists in the template is the field itself in the round-tripped document.
trajectory.produces: A merge template whose placeholders have been confirmed present.

trajectory.action: Merge all fourteen records one per page with each room's own photograph bound through the image column and the agent's own tinted frames supplied as the image files, render for the printer, and then look at every card at trim.
trajectory.judgement: Page count equals row count on a run where fields are missing and copy is cut off, so counting pages proves nothing. Looking at all fourteen rather than the first is the agent's own decision.
trajectory.produces: A fourteen-page press file plus per-record files, and a verdict on every card.

trajectory.action: Create the board and add the finished set for the client's partner, treating a partial success as partial. Then write the note: per frame what was applied, the tint hue, strength and grain, the exception held out of the treatment, the type system, anything licensed, every resize or extension reported, and any frame that could not be brought into the set.
trajectory.judgement: What to escalate rather than quietly fix. A frame dropped from the set changes which picture carries which page, and the client needs to hear that from the freelancer rather than find it.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the committed tone actually does to this particular set. A single tone ramp maps every colour in a frame onto one hue, so any frame whose subject is told apart from its ground by hue rather than by value loses that separation completely. Two of these detail frames are exactly that case (a moss-green throw on an oak-grey bench, a terracotta cup on a rust-red tray) and both collapse into one flat field. Nothing in either photograph announces it: they look like ordinary detail shots, they look correct in colour, the tint operation reports success, and each tinted file still reads as plausibly moody on its own at thumbnail size. The collapse only exists as a comparison against the rest of the set at reproduction size. The strength that carries the other frames is also the strength that kills these two, so there is no single setting that resolves it.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot dodge it and care cannot pre-empt it: which frames depend on hue for separation is a property of what was in the room that day, and it cannot be read off a colour preview, since in colour both frames separate perfectly well. (b) Nothing states it. The brief asks for one tone across every amenity and detail shot and names the single true-colour exception it already knows about; it says nothing about any frame failing, and no asset note or earlier step identifies these two. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the response is to go back before the tint and build luminance separation that was never there, by lifting or dropping one side under a mask, or to accept that these two frames are not treatable and change which frames carry which pages.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Return to the corrected base for those frames and separate subject from ground by value under a mask before re-committing the tone, then re-tint and look at the set again rather than assuming the second attempt took. Check the frames that were not flagged at the same reproduction size, since the reason to look was found on two frames and the rest have not been established as clean. If a frame will not separate without looking manipulated, drop it and re-plan the lookbook around the frames that survive.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The lookbook opens on two grey mush frames in the middle of a set that is supposed to be the property's entire point of difference, and they go out on the social canvases as well, in front of exactly the design-literate booker the direct-booking channel was built to reach.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the cut-outs hold where they are actually used. The carafe is unglazed and was styled against the hotel's own limewashed plaster, so on its shadow side the object and the ground sit at effectively the same value. The knockout succeeds, returns a clean-looking transparent file, and has quietly taken the lip and part of the shoulder with it. On white and on any pale layout that missing edge is invisible, because what is gone was pale anyway; on the near-black booking ground it reads as a bite out of the silhouette. Which of the three objects does this, and how far the bite runs, is a property of the styling in that one photograph rather than of the route chosen or the care taken, and no tool reports edge quality at all.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it: the cut-outs have to be made regardless of sequence, there is no metadata that describes an edge, and the defect does not exist in the returned file in isolation, only in relation to the ground it is composited on. (b) Nothing states it. The client says every version they tried looks fine until it goes on the dark, which is a client describing the symptom that made them hire somebody, not a statement of which object, why, or that the cause is a shared value on one side. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the fix is a different operation on a different principle, selecting the plaster as a material and inverting rather than asking for the object, and it carries a further decision about whether the object needs restyling advice back to the client rather than a cut.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-cut the affected object by naming the ground material and inverting rather than by asking for the subject, re-composite on the near-black ground and inspect the same edge again rather than assuming the second route worked, and inspect the other two objects at the same magnification, since one object having been caught is not evidence about the others. If an edge cannot be recovered, say so and propose the object be reshot on a ground that separates, rather than shipping a bitten silhouette.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The booking page, the one page the entire launch exists to convert on, carries a carafe with a chunk missing from its side, which is the precise defect the client hired someone to fix, handed back as fixed.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the fourteen merged cards are actually complete at trim. Last season's card was set around the shortest room name the hotel had, and three rooms were renamed this season with longer names and longer view lines. A merged record that exceeds its frame does not spill, does not wrap onto the card and does not raise anything: it simply stops rendering at the frame edge, so the card comes back looking like a properly composed card that happens to name a room slightly differently. Every automatic signal passes: the merge reports success, the page count equals the row count, the pages are in the printer's order and each card carries the correct room photograph. The frame's true capacity at the merged type size is not published anywhere and cannot be computed from the printed card, so the only way to know is to merge and look at all fourteen.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it and care cannot pre-empt it: capacity depends on the frame geometry the conversion produced and the type size the template carries, neither of which is knowable before the merge exists, and comparing string lengths against last year's copy gives no threshold. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says the room list changes and hands over a spreadsheet with the new rates and views, which is a client describing their content, not disclosing that three records overrun. No asset note in the client's hands names the rooms and no acceptance line explains the cause. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the response is a decision the client has to be involved in, shorten the copy, move the long field to a frame that can hold it, or change the type treatment on the card, and each of those changes the mapping and the design rather than repeating an operation on changed input.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Identify which records are cut, decide with the copy in hand whether the fix is an editorial shortening, a re-mapping so the long field lands in a frame with slack, or a type change on the card, then rebuild the mapping, re-confirm the placeholders in the round-tripped document, re-merge and look at all fourteen again rather than only the three that were caught.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Fourteen room cards go to the printer and sit on the desks of a hotel that charges six hundred a night with three of them naming the room half way through a word, discovered by guests rather than by anyone at the hotel.

deliverables.name: Nordhaven signature image set
deliverables.spec: The property shoot brought from two separate visits onto one base and then carried to a single committed tone with one tint hue, one strength and one grain across the whole set, plus the one true-colour room hero for the booking page held deliberately out of the treatment, every output at or below its source dimensions, with per-frame applied settings, every resize or edge extension any tool reported, and any frame that could not be brought into the set named along with what happened to the placement it was carrying. Delivered at the placement crops composed for the size each is used at, which are part of this one set rather than separate deliverables.

deliverables.name: Amenity cut-outs for the booking page
deliverables.spec: The carafe, the robe and the key fob as genuinely transparent artwork whose edges hold on the near-black ground the booking page uses, judged on that ground rather than on white, with no edge bitten away where object and ground share value and no enclosed interior left filled with captured material. Each delivered both transparent and composited on the house ground, with the route used per object stated, and any object that cannot be cut cleanly named with what to do instead.

deliverables.name: Lookbook, social and story canvases as one editable document plus its source
deliverables.spec: A single native editable Express document carrying the lookbook spread, the 4:5 social canvas and the 9:16 story canvas, each keeping its own canvas size, with live editable text in one licensed type system and every photograph carried as embedded image data rather than as a reference. Delivered with the self-contained source it was authored from, because the room list changes and the client edits this themselves.

deliverables.name: Fourteen room directory cards

decision_gates: Which single frame is the true-colour exception, and holding it out of the treatment when the headline ask is consistency.
How far the tone is pushed, given that at this band restraint is the design and the same strength that carries most frames destroys the ones that separate by hue.
Whether both visits are brought onto one base before the style is committed, or the style is committed on top of two different bases.
Where a global correction stops working and the move has to be masked to a named material rather than to the object sitting on it.
Whether a frame that collapses under the tone is rescued by building value separation or dropped from the set, and which page then carries which picture.
Knockout route per object rather than per batch, given that one of the three cannot be knocked out by background removal at all.
On which ground the cut-out edges are judged, when both failure modes are invisible on white.
Whether to extend a frame at its edges or accept a tighter crop, knowing extended material has to match the tone that was already committed.
Whether the licensed exterior joins the set under the committed tone, judged on luminance structure rather than on colour, and what to do if it does not.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a six-hundred-dollar property rather than a booking platform listing.
Whether the mapping can be done per frame at all, or whether the conversion forces everything through offsets inside one story.
What to do about a record that overruns its frame: shorten the copy, re-map the field, or change the card's type treatment, and which of those needs the client's agreement.
What to escalate in writing versus what to fix silently, on a job whose deliverables go straight to a printer and a live booking page.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns pictures of a hotel that does not exist. IDENTITY is the commission: these are sixteen frames of one specific building, one specific carafe and one specific brass fob, and the entire direct-booking proposition is that the guest is seeing this property rather than a generic mood. A regenerated interior is a misrepresentation on a booking page, which is a legal problem and not only a craft one. SPEC: the deliverables are defined by surfaces and numbers a generation cannot satisfy, genuine partial-alpha transparency that survives on a named near-black ground, crops composed at named delivered sizes with no output larger than its source, and fourteen cards at one record per page in the printer's order carrying the correct room's photograph. EDITABILITY: the lookbook set exists as a deliverable because the client edits it themselves as the room list changes, so it has to arrive as a native document with live text and real photographs, not as a flat picture of a layout. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: does this frame still separate once the tone is committed, does this edge hold on the ground it will actually sit on, does this record still fit its frame at trim. None of that is a generation problem, and none of it can be checked by looking at a render.
doability_proof: Five surfaces, honestly counted, none padded: the Illustrator tools are never called because document_render_vector and document_merge_data_vector sit on a polling helper that does not exist in this host, and no video or audio tool is invoked for the same reason. Every link is verified in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account). IMAGING: auto_straighten, auto_tone, masked and unmasked image_apply_adjustments, monochromatic_tint and add_grain (both mask-accepting), select_by_prompt and select_subject with returnBbox, invert_selection, fill_area, remove_background in both the transparent and the backgroundColor forms, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs array and generative_expand are all verified headless. Transparent RGBA with genuinely feathered partial alpha is verified and survives both crop tools at png output, which is what the cut-out deliverable depends on, and the documented rule that outputFileType must stay png through the whole chain is why one jpeg step would destroy it. remove_background is documented as unable to punch an enclosed interior (it returned a solid opaque disc on the ring badge probe), which is exactly why the fob needs the select, invert and fill route instead, and it is documented as silently downscaling oversized inputs and reporting it only as a tradeoff, which is why the no-invented-pixels bar is scored as a decision plus a disclosure rather than as a measurement. The prompt-wording asymmetry, where naming the substrate returns the substrate and naming a material's own visual properties returns the material, is a verified live finding and is what the masked plaster and oak corrections turn on. crop_and_resize is documented as interpolating to a hard 2x cap and reporting it only in tradeoffs. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export are verified, external image URLs render as empty grey boxes so every photograph is embedded as image data, the right-anchored auto-sized wrapper failure and the non-inherited font weight are verified live findings the trajectory designs against, and canvasWidth, canvasHeight and slideSelector are never passed as tool params because they are global overrides that collapse a mixed-size set. Transport goes through the text/html upload path because embedded photography passes the inline threshold, and verification is split because the rendition preview shows the first canvas only. Persistence is not assumed, so the deliverable is the editable document plus the self-contained source. INDESIGN: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout and document_render_layout are all verified fully headless and synchronous, a merge template built out of a bare press PDF is verified end to end, one record per page is the confirmed PDF behaviour with page count equal to row count, and per-row image binding through an at-prefixed CSV column plus additionalImageFiles is verified visually. The documented lossy textContent readout, the validator returning VALID on wrong offsets, prepare reporting success while dropping mappings, and the frame granularity of a converted PDF not matching its printed blocks are all verified live findings, which is why the trajectory reconstructs the story text and re-exports IDML to confirm placeholders. Per-record files come from createSeparateFiles or a recordRange loop because multi-record raster output is documented as returning in reversed order with lying labels. No bleed gate and no named press preset is specified, since both are documented as unobtainable from a PDF-sourced template, and no variable QR appears anywhere. FONTS: the recommend, styles, find, kit chain is verified end to end in a real browser, and the non-standard numeric weights, the display-cut-by-slug rule, the slug-not-PostScript CSS rule and the all-or-nothing kit call are live findings the task leans on. STOCK AND BOARDS: short generic queries only because long queries return zero hits, the orientation filter is broken and never passed, licensing returns genuine camera-scale imagery, and boards persist with a twelve-placement cap where 201 means partial success with a failed-items list. VOLUME: twenty-one client files in, roughly thirty-eight artefacts moved in total, every multi-image call at or under the ten-item cap and no batch above twenty. AVOIDED: no text-to-image, no generative fill, no AI object removal, no background-replace-by-prompt, no upscaling, no OCR, no compositing, no fill_text, no animate_design, no create_firefly_board, no replace_image, no download_design, and no photograph reaching Express as a URL.
